accepted.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
accepted.scope: CPU primitives implement Pareto layers, explicit-quota blending, set-dependent pipeline deltas, remove/refill trimming and admission of completed validation trials. FI, cost oracle, removal order and measured trials are external. No LLM feature proposer, FI estimator, asynchronous research controller or production launch runs. This is not a complete agentic optimizer.
accepted.cost_basis: Real trial evaluation takes hours to days; a session contains about10–25 trials with4–8 concurrent jobs, private feature outcomes, fleet budget services and production rankers. The complete campaign exceeds one A100/A30 or Mac budget. Explicit-input CPU primitives should take under30seconds across three seeds, with no model/data downloads or API calls.
accepted.component_budget: Expected less than30seconds/three seeds; no model/data downloads or API calls.

accepted.title: DNA: Unlocking Depth Scaling in CTR Models
accepted.scope: Executes small differentiable attention, group-specific projections, token-specific SwiGLUs, composite request projections and D-1 updates. Controls compare batched/individual candidates, padding invariance, request-dependent history and finite gradients. score returns logits, not click probabilities; BCEWithLogits stably incorporates Eq13's sigmoid. Local QKNorm is per-head L2 normalization times learned scales. Width/depth are reduced. Explicit generated tokens replace HHFT inputs; private CTR training, the512-wide production model and serving benchmarks are absent. Fixture BCE is not CTR capability.
accepted.cost_basis: Paper DNA-4 has roughly1.267B dense parameters excluding embedding tables, width512, eight heads, thousand-token histories, private Taobao training and multiple depth/compute comparisons. Full training/A/B is not reproduced. Tiny CPU/CUDA three-seed mechanisms should take under30seconds without model/data downloads or APIs.
accepted.component_budget: Expected less than30seconds/three seeds; no model/data downloads or API calls.

accepted.title: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation
accepted.scope: Only point-in-time slicing and completed-vector selection. Callers must isolate events/records to one user and apply eligibility/catalog mapping first: there is no user_id authorization boundary or complete production leakage defense. Missing required vectors need external cold start; missing/disabled LLM pairs require compatible baseline fusion, not automatic changes to treatment input dimensions. Greatest-as_of selection and dropping incomplete LLM pairs are local handoff safeguards, not prescribed TTL/fallback algorithms. There is no BGE/Qwen encoder,16-layer decoder, InfoNCE training, private receipts, real store, ANN or learned cold start. No vectors are fabricated; encoder_calls is always0. This is L0, not retrieval capability.
accepted.cost_basis: The full path includes a frozen0.6B text embedding model, an adapted Qwen3-style16-layer/four-head event decoder, private multicontent label receipts, two-tower training, SageMaker serving and production experiments. Private contracts and the campaign exceed this short single-device budget. CPU protocol cases should take under30seconds/three seeds without model/data downloads or APIs.
accepted.component_budget: Expected less than30seconds/three seeds; no model/data downloads or API calls.
